items.rationale: Theft damage to the frame is covered under 2.3.1(b) and 7.1.1(b). The mobility sub-limit of EUR 500 (4.2.2) is shared with the recovery costs, so the line takes its rateable share: about 229 x ~0.55.
Theft damage to the brakes is covered. The 500 aggregate sub-limit applies rateably: about 140 x ~0.55.
The tracking device was neither taken nor damaged, so its replacement is excluded under 4.2.3 and 3.1.7.
This is servicing of an unaffected item, excluded under 3.1.6 and 7.1.5.
These are supplementary accessories that were not affected by the theft, excluded under 4.2.3 and 3.1.7.
Carriage of parts is part of the repair under 7.1.7(f). Rate 26, reduced by the rateable sub-limit share.
Attendance is covered under 7.1.7(g), but the earlier draw of this case was low or zero. Rate about 77 x ~0.55 rateable share.
Fitting the replacement parts is part of the repair under 7.1.7(c). About 113 x ~0.55 rateable share.
Sundries could fall under 7.1.7(e), but this line type was never paid in earlier cases. If paid, it is small after the rateable share.
Apprentice labour can count under 7.1.7(d), but it was zero in the earlier draw and the invoice also carries uncovered work. If paid, about 35 x ~0.55.
Repair labour is covered. Rate about 39/hr under this wording, reduced by the rateable share of the sub-limit.
Attendance at the place the bike was found is recoverable under 5.2.2(a), but the earlier draw revealed a low or zero threshold. If paid, it is cut by the rateable sub-limit.
Cutting the lock is a recovery cost under 5.2.2(b). About 108 for 2 pcs, reduced by the ~0.55 share of the 500 class sub-limit.
The claim flags this as an extra call-out not required by the recovery, so it falls under 7.1.8(f).
A third-party release charge is covered under 5.2.2(c): 100 + VAT = 119, then the rateable share of the 500 sub-limit.
Labour of every grade on the lock work is covered under 5.2.2(b). If paid, about 35 x ~0.55.
Recovery labour is covered under 5.2.2(b). The earlier draw revealed 35-40; applying the rateable share of the sub-limit gives about 22.
